newsitem.title: UK: UK's Thorn shares slide as turnover falls.
newsitem.headline: UK's Thorn shares slide as turnover falls.

text.p: Shares in British rentals company Thorn Plc fell almost 12 percent on Monday after the company said first quarter turnover had dropped by 8.5 percent.
The shares slid 21 pence to 156p at 1210 GMT after the comments from outgoing Thorn chairman Sir Colin Southgate at the company's annual meeting.

Southgate told shareholders that the strength of the pound would reduce reported profits this year by around 11 million pounds ($18.6 million) at current rates. First quarter turnover fell by one percent when measured at constant currency rates.
Southgate, who as planned stepped down to be replaced by deputy chairman Hugh Jenkins on Monday, said the current year would be "challenging" for the company.
Share analysts said the statement was likely to prompt downgrading of profit forecasts.
"The figures are a touch on the disappointing side in terms of UK trading and the foreign exchange hit," said Nick Bubb of brokers SocGen.
"Our expectations were at 140 (million profit before tax) for the year and on the face of it that could be on the high side," he added.

Thorn split from music company EMI Group Plc in a demerger last August. Its shares, which started life at 408 pence, have performed poorly on worries over trading and litigation relating to U.S. rental agreements.
Shareholders approved changes to the company's capital structure, paving the way for it to return some 87 million pounds to investors under a scheme unveiled when it announced 1996 results in May.

The company said its Radio Rentals British high street video and television stores had been hit by higher insurance tax rates. Radio Rentals revenues were 8.9 percent lower year-on-year as at the end of June.
The number of cancellations rose 20 percent, an increase blamed on the tax hike and windfall payments from building society flotations which have boosted sales of consumer goods.
Southgate said its Crazy George's chain which rent households items including furniture to low income consumers was among activities which it planned to develop.

In a separate statement, the company dismissed a newspaper report alleging interest charges on some of Crazy George's rental packages could be as high as 80 percent annually. It said they were 29.9 percent as advertised.
Britain's Office of Fair Trading confirmed that local trading standards officers had raised concerns about Crazy George's but would not give any details. ($ = 0.591 British Pounds)
